scope: First-principles and civil-application review for the learning journey. No real sensor performance, operational constellation state, or cooler rating is inferred. Scene geometry and playback remain representative.
result: No arithmetic correction was needed in the existing orbit, photon-energy, Planck-band, diffraction, or Carnot functions. The principal gaps were explanatory behavior and animation semantics.

findings.finding: Earth and GEO already co-rotate correctly in the illustration. Other orbit-family markers were static. The authored compressed HEO ellipse and the independent physical teaching HEO have different eccentricities.
findings.action: Use each drawing guide's own parameters for its moving marker. Advance mean anomaly uniformly and solve Kepler's equation; do not use uniform true anomaly or silently combine different ellipse shapes. Keep the accelerated illustration clock distinct from real elapsed orbital time.
findings.implementation: Pure helpers added in src/model/orbits.ts; scene integration belongs to the animation work. No physical orbital inputs were changed.

findings.finding: All layers used a common fractional path clock. Catmull-Rom tension zero does keep each segment straight, but its zero tangents ease the glyph to zero speed at every vertex.
findings.action: Distinguish optical propagation, data sequence, and thermal energy transfer. Use arclength for optical glyphs and identify illustrative timing. Do not draw heat-transfer glyphs as actual refrigerant trajectories or imply a pulse-tube cooler circulates gas continuously in one direction.
sourceRefs: PDF pp. 6–7, section F1.3; PDF p. 14, section F1.3.2, oscillating pressures and mass flows

findings.finding: Detector choice has no quantitative output; this is scientifically appropriate without device-specific inputs. The old scenario listener nevertheless rebuilt every scene and reset selection, including when only a reference choice changed.
findings.action: Present material choices as a reference catalog, explain the missing dependencies, and preserve the current scene, selected part, and camera when changing independent teaching inputs. Do not invent a temperature or spectral-response curve from a material name.
findings.implementation: Finding handed to the learning-control owner; no scene or UI changes made by this audit.

findings.action: Show Qhot = Qcold + Win as a complete-cycle energy balance. The warm side rejects absorbed heat plus supplied work. Startup or cooldown requires an additional stored-energy term. This identity alone cannot determine a real cooler's capacity or efficiency.
findings.implementation: Added coolerEnergyBalance(heatRemoved, inputWork), with no defaults or mission values, and registered the symbolic equation with its boundary assumption.

findings.action: An explicit ideal-source temperature control would make the existing Planck curve more instructive; an aperture-only laboratory control could show inverse aperture scaling. Each would require its own visible assumed input and evidence row. Neither should compute military image resolution, detector counts, thresholds, or performance.
findings.implementation: Not implemented. The existing fixed source and aperture remain unchanged; no arbitrary new nominal inputs were added.

equations.boundary: Ideal ellipse, focus at origin, pericenter on positive x. Coordinate units follow a. Drawing parameters are not a spacecraft ephemeris.
